reports.title: Leah Ratheram
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Adults aged between 18 - 25 now have mental health services provided by two organisations - Forward Thinking Birmingham and Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Trust. If a patient presents in crisis to A&E they will be seen by someone from the RAID team who work for Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Trust. If they require ongoing treatment they will be referred to forward Thinking Birmingham. There is a concern that patients will have no coordinated approach to their care at a time of crisis
concerns.hazard: lack of coordinated care for young adults

concerns.quote: Both organisations use different record keeping systems. There is a real risk that information will not be shared effectively and key risk factors will be missed in the handover process. It was unclear how staff from each organisation would access each other's records when patients present to one or other of the services.

The Mental Health Act assessment process was followed in this case was unclear. An approved social worked declined to be involved until the assessment had been completed. There is a concern that lack of involvement of this speciality at any early stage will affect the quality of mental health act assessments and the safety of patients.
concerns.hazard: lack of early involvement of approved social worker

reports.title: Peter Fleming: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: There continues to be a chronic lack of resources to treat seriously mentally ill patients in Birmingham and Solihull
communication between the specialist teams is not effective enough
Carbamazepine management was proposed in 2012 to manage the deceased's mental health however this was not picked up by his GP and was only noted by a BSMHFT consultant in August 2022
different health organisations use different digital systems that do not communicate with each other
current resources do not allow GPs to pro- actively check patients are collecting prescribed medication due to excessive patient lists

reports.title: Lauren Bridges (1): Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: All Integrated Care Boards (ICBs) were asked to work towards eliminating the practice in NHS England's 2023/24 Priorities and Operational Planning Guidance.

The Trust has undertaken a comprehensive review to ensure that all patients who are receiving acute care funded by the Trust in Out of Area beds are accurately identified as such on our clinical system.
promises.summary: Identify all out-of-area patients receiving acute care on clinical system

promises.quote: We have enhanced the daily Hospital Overview situation report which is accurate at the point it is sent, with the purpose of providing a summary at the start of the working day across the organisation to key colleagues including senior clinicians and managers.
In addition, the Trust has also added a specific section to the daily Hospital Overview template showing patients who are in out of area beds who require repatriation to a local bed.
promises.summary: Add repatriation section to daily Hospital Overview

promises.quote: We have updated the electronic admission form template that is embedded in the patient record system so that when a patient requires admission, we capture more robust information, which is then also reportable in a bed state automated report.

The Trust has implemented a new Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Enabling Purposeful Admissions. This clearly sets out the required process, roles and responsibilities of key staff and the required recording in respect of inpatient flow decisions.

We have reviewed our daily clinical meeting that takes place in respect of bed flow and set out requirements in the meeting's terms of reference, including standard items for discussion and recording standards.
promises.summary: Review daily clinical meeting terms of reference

concerns.quote: This is the second inquest I have heard where the delayed discharge/repatriation of an Out-of-Area patient from an independent provider's hospital has been a contributory factor in that patient's death
The jury identified inadequate and insufficient communication between Dorset Healthcare NHS Trust, The Priory and relevant parties
There is no national standard process for referrals into the independent sector nor for discharge/repatriation to the 'home team'
The Priory deals with 42 NHS separate commissioning bodies
multiple software programmes for record keeping for these organisations, which makes transfer and sharing of clinical information cumbersome and difficult, as direct sharing is not possible
